Penalties Guide

The Complete Guide to T2 Late Filing Penalties

How the percentage penalty is calculated, why a nil return is different, the paper and preparer penalties, and what an unfiled year costs. Nil T2 filing is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOWCatch-Up Nil T2 Filing

Last reviewed: October 22, 2026  ·  All nil T2 filing guides

On this page

  1. How the Percentage Penalty Is Calculated
  2. Why a Nil Return Is Different
  3. The Larger Penalty for a Repeated Failure
  4. The Paper Filing Penalty and the Preparer Penalty
  5. The Non-Resident Penalty of $25.00 a Day
  6. What a Demand to File Changes
  7. Arbitrary Assessment
  8. Interest, and What It Attaches To
  9. What an Open Year Blocks
  10. How Long an Unfiled Year Stays Open
  11. Filing the Missing Years
  12. What the Fee Covers

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

How the Percentage Penalty Is Calculated

The late-filing penalty on a T2 is a percentage of the tax owing on the return. It is 5% of the unpaid tax, plus 1% of that unpaid tax for each complete month the return is late, to a maximum of 12 months.

ElementAmount
Base penalty5% of the unpaid tax
Monthly addition1% of the unpaid tax per complete month late
Maximum months counted12
Applied toTax owing on the return, not revenue and not assets

Every figure above is a percentage of one number: the tax owing. That is the whole reason a nil return behaves differently.

Why a Nil Return Is Different

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

Both halves of that statement are true at once, and neither is useful on its own. A corporation owing $0.00 has nothing for the percentage to be a percentage of. The same corporation still has an open year on its record, and that is what the rest of this guide is about.

See whether a nil T2 can be filed late for the short answer.

The Larger Penalty for a Repeated Failure

Where the Canada Revenue Agency has already issued a demand to file, and a late-filing penalty was charged in any of the three preceding tax years, the penalty doubles.

SituationBaseMonthlyMaximum months
First late return5%1%12
Repeated failure after a demand10%2%20

It is still a percentage of tax owing, so a nil year still produces $0.00 under it. A corporation that is nil in one year and trading in the next is the one this rule catches.

The Paper Filing Penalty and the Preparer Penalty

For tax years starting after 2023 electronic filing is mandatory for virtually all corporations. A paper T2 draws a $1,000.00 penalty plus a $100.00 per-return preparer penalty.

This is the one penalty on this page that is not a percentage of tax owing. It is a flat amount, and a nil return is not exempt from it. A corporation with no activity that files on paper is exposed to the full $1,000.00.

Returns are transmitted electronically here, by a registered EFILE electronic filer.

Nil T2 Filing, $300.00 plus HST per tax year

One price for every year and every province. CPA reviewed and transmitted electronically.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

The Non-Resident Penalty of $25.00 a Day

A non-resident-owned corporation that fails to file faces a penalty built on days rather than on tax owing: $25.00 per day, to a maximum of $2,500.00.

Because it is not a percentage, a nil year reaches the maximum exactly as a trading year does. It is the single largest exposure a dormant non-resident-owned corporation carries.

What a Demand to File Changes

A demand to file is a formal written requirement to file a named return by a named date. It converts an overdue return into a legal obligation with its own deadline, and it starts the clock on the repeated-failure rate above.

The response is covered in full in the guide to responding to a CRA demand to file.

Arbitrary Assessment

Where a demand goes unanswered, the Canada Revenue Agency may assess the corporation on its own estimate of income. That assessment is a real debt, collectible, and it stands until it is displaced by a filed return.

An arbitrary assessment is how a corporation that owed $0.00 ends up owing a figure with interest running on it. The amount is an estimate the corporation did not provide and cannot be argued down without filing the actual return.

Interest, and What It Attaches To

Interest is charged on an unpaid balance, compounded daily. A nil return produces no balance, so there is nothing for interest to run on.

ChargeAttaches toOn a true nil year
Percentage late-filing penaltyTax owing$0.00
InterestAn unpaid balance$0.00
Paper filing penaltyThe filing method$1,000.00 if filed on paper
Preparer penaltyEach paper return prepared$100.00
Non-resident penaltyDays lateUp to $2,500.00

Read the table by column rather than by row. Two of the five charges ignore tax owing entirely.

What an Open Year Blocks

An unfiled year blocks a clearance certificate, and a clearance certificate is what a corporation needs before it can be wound up cleanly. It also stops a voluntary dissolution from completing.

The sequence is set out in the guide to the final T2 and dissolution.

How Long an Unfiled Year Stays Open

Indefinitely. There is no point at which an unfiled T2 year closes itself, and no number of later filings that settles an earlier gap.

This is why the cost of an unfiled nil year is almost never the penalty. It is the demand, the arbitrary assessment, the blocked clearance certificate and the dissolution that cannot complete.

Filing the Missing Years

Unfiled years are filed oldest first, each on its own return for its own tax year. Five unfiled nil years are five returns, and they can be prepared and transmitted together.

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

See the guide to catching up on unfiled corporate tax returns.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is There a Penalty for Filing a Nil T2 Late?

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

How Is the T2 Late-Filing Penalty Worked Out?

5% of the unpaid tax, plus 1% of that unpaid tax for each complete month the return is late, counted to a maximum of 12 months. Every component is a percentage of tax owing.

What Is the Penalty for Filing a T2 on Paper?

For tax years starting after 2023 electronic filing is mandatory for virtually all corporations. A paper T2 draws a $1,000.00 penalty plus a $100.00 per-return preparer penalty. A nil return is not exempt from either.

When Does the Penalty Rate Double?

Where the Canada Revenue Agency has issued a demand to file and a late-filing penalty was charged in any of the three preceding tax years. The rate becomes 10% plus 2% per complete month, to 20 months.

What Happens if I Ignore a Demand to File?

The Canada Revenue Agency may assess the corporation on its own estimate of income. That arbitrary assessment is collectible and stands until the actual return displaces it.

Does an Unfiled Year Ever Close on Its Own?

No. An unfiled T2 year stays open indefinitely, and later filings do not settle an earlier gap.

Demand to File Guide

The Complete Guide to Responding to a CRA Demand to File

What a demand to file is, the deadline it sets, what happens if it is ignored, and how an arbitrary assessment is displaced by filing. Nil T2 filing is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

On this page

  1. What a Demand to File Is

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What a Demand to File Is

A written requirement from the Canada Revenue Agency that a named return be filed by a named date. It is not a reminder and it is not an assessment. It is a legal obligation with its own deadline, separate from the original filing deadline the return already missed.

A demand is usually the first contact a dormant corporation receives. Nothing has gone to collections at this point, and the position is still straightforward to resolve.

Why It Arrived

Because the Canada Revenue Agency holds a record showing the corporation exists and a tax year for which no return was received. Incorporation created that record, and it persists whether or not the corporation ever traded.

TriggerWhat the Agency sees
Incorporated and never tradedAn open tax year with no return
Stopped trading, kept the corporationA gap after the last return filed
An open RC accountA filing obligation on the account
A year-end passing with no returnThe corporation moving into arrears

None of the four requires the corporation to have earned anything.

Reading the Letter

Three things on the letter decide what happens next: which tax year or years are named, the date the return is required by, and whether the letter names a specific officer of the corporation.

The named date is the one that matters. A demand answered by that date closes the matter. A demand answered late is treated as a repeated failure, which doubles the percentage penalty rate on any year where tax is owing.

A Nil Year Still Answers the Demand

Filing a nil return satisfies a demand in exactly the way a trading return does. The obligation is to file, not to owe.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

See what happens where a demand to file goes unanswered.

Nil T2 Filing, $300.00 plus HST per tax year

One price for every year and every province. CPA reviewed and transmitted electronically.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

What Happens if It Is Ignored

The Canada Revenue Agency proceeds without the corporation. It may assess on its own estimate of income, and in a persistent case may pursue the failure through the courts.

StageWhat it means
Demand issuedA deadline to file is set
Demand unansweredThe repeated-failure penalty rate becomes available
Arbitrary assessmentA tax debt is raised on an estimate
CollectionThat debt is pursued like any other
ProsecutionAvailable where the failure persists

The corporation moves down that table by doing nothing.

How an Arbitrary Assessment Works

The Agency estimates income from whatever it holds, assesses tax on that estimate, and issues a notice. The figure is not a guess the corporation can correct by explaining; it is an assessment that stands until a filed return replaces it.

Interest runs on the assessed balance from the date it is raised. For a corporation that genuinely had no activity, this is how a year that owed $0.00 becomes a debt.

Displacing an Arbitrary Assessment

By filing the actual return for that year. The filed return is assessed on its own figures and supersedes the estimate.

A nil return displaces an arbitrary assessment to $0.00 where the corporation truly had no activity. The sooner it is filed, the less interest has accumulated on the estimate in the meantime.

Where the Demand Names Several Years

Each year named is a separate return on its own form for its own tax year. Five years named is five returns. They are prepared and transmitted together, oldest first.

See whether five years of nil T2 returns can be filed at once.

Checking the Year Really Was Nil

Before filing, the year is tested rather than assumed. A corporation is nil for this service only where it had no activity at all in the tax year.

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Share capital, cash, a shareholder loan, an incorporation cost or a bank charge does not stop the year being nil, but it does make GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required. The detail is in the guide to GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141.

The Accounts a T2 Does Not Close

Answering a demand for a T2 settles the corporate income tax obligation and nothing else. An open GST/HST account and an open payroll account each carry their own filing obligations and generate their own demands.

A GST/HST account is closed with Form RC145. Until it is closed or filed nil, it keeps producing letters of its own.

After the Return Is Transmitted

The confirmation of transmission is the record that the demand was answered. It is kept with the corporation’s minute book alongside the assessment that follows.

Where the corporation is being wound up, the clearance certificate is applied for only once every open year has been filed. That order is set out in the guide to the final T2 and dissolution.

Frequently Asked Questions

What Is a CRA Demand to File?

A written requirement from the Canada Revenue Agency that a named return be filed by a named date. It sets its own deadline, separate from the filing deadline the return already missed.

Does Filing a Nil Return Answer a Demand?

Yes. The obligation is to file, not to owe. A nil return satisfies a demand in the same way a trading return does.

What if I Ignore It?

The Canada Revenue Agency may assess the corporation on its own estimate of income. That arbitrary assessment is a collectible debt with interest running on it, and it stands until a filed return displaces it.

Can an Arbitrary Assessment Be Reversed?

It is displaced rather than argued down. Filing the actual return for that year replaces the estimate, and a genuine nil year displaces it to $0.00.

The Demand Names Four Years. Is That Four Returns?

Yes. Each tax year is its own return on its own form. They are prepared and transmitted together, oldest first.

Does Answering the Demand Close My GST/HST Account?

No. A T2 settles the corporate income tax obligation only. An open GST/HST account carries its own filing obligation and is closed with Form RC145.

Holding Company Guide

The Complete Guide to Inactive Holding Company Filing

When a holding corporation is nil and when it is not, what investment income does to the return, and which schedules a holding company needs. Nil T2 filing is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOWInactive Holding Corporation Filing

Last reviewed: October 22, 2026  ·  All nil T2 filing guides

On this page

  1. A Holding Corporation With Investment Income Is Not Nil
  2. When a Holding Corporation Genuinely Is Nil
  3. The Interest Trap
  4. An Inactive Holding Corporation Still Files
  5. The Schedules a Holding Corporation Needs
  6. Schedule 50 in a Holding Structure
  7. Inter-Company Transactions
  8. Dividends, In and Out
  9. A Holding Corporation Held in Reserve

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

A Holding Corporation With Investment Income Is Not Nil

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Read that before anything else on this page. Most corporations described as “an inactive holding company” turn out to hold something that earns, and earning is activity. Interest credited on a balance is income. A dividend received is income. Rent is income.

This guide covers both cases, and says plainly which one a corporation is in. It does not try to make the second case into the first.

When a Holding Corporation Genuinely Is Nil

Where it held assets that earned nothing at all during the tax year, received no dividend, paid no dividend, had no revenue of any kind, claimed no expense, ran no payroll, bought no asset and had no inter-company transaction.

In the tax yearNilNot nil
Shares held, no dividend receivedNil
Shares held, dividend receivedNot nil
Cash in an account earning no interestNil
Cash in an account earning interestNot nil
Property held, no rent chargedNil
Property rented outNot nil
A dividend paid up to the shareholderNot nil
A loan to a related corporation, no interestNil
A loan to a related corporation, interest chargedNot nil

The left column is the whole of the nil case. One entry in the right column takes the corporation out of it.

The Interest Trap

The most common reason a holding corporation believed to be nil is not nil is a few dollars of interest credited on a bank balance nobody looked at.

There is no minimum. Interest of $4.12 credited across the year is investment income, and the corporation is not nil for that year. It is checked on the statements rather than assumed from memory.

An Inactive Holding Corporation Still Files

Every resident corporation, including an inactive one, must file a T2 within six months of its fiscal year-end, every year, until it is formally dissolved. A final T2 is due within six months of dissolution.

Holding structures are frequently left for years on the assumption that a corporation doing nothing owes nothing to anyone. The obligation is to file, not to owe.

One price for every year and every province. CPA reviewed and transmitted electronically.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

The Schedules a Holding Corporation Needs

A holding corporation almost always has a balance sheet, which is what decides the schedules.

ScheduleWhen it is required
GIFI 100, 125 and 141Where there is share capital, cash, a shareholder loan, an incorporation cost or a bank charge
Schedule 50For every shareholder at 10% or more
Schedule 24On the first return after incorporation
Schedule 8 and loss continuityRecorded

A corporation inactive all year with nothing at all to report may omit GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141, but any share capital, cash, shareholder loan, incorporation cost or bank charge makes them required. A holding corporation holds things by definition, so the exemption rarely reaches it.

Schedule 50 in a Holding Structure

Schedule 50 is needed for any shareholder at 10% or more, and holding structures concentrate ownership, so it is almost always required.

Where the shareholder is itself a corporation, the row records that corporation and its business number rather than an individual. The detail is in the guide to Schedule 8 and loss continuity and on the Schedule 50 and the 10% shareholder rule post.

Inter-Company Transactions

A transfer between a holding corporation and an operating corporation is a transaction, and a year containing one is not nil. That includes a management fee charged, a loan advanced on interest, and an expense paid by one and borne by the other.

An interest-free loan outstanding across the year, with nothing moving and nothing charged, does not by itself make the year active. It does put a balance on the balance sheet, which makes the GIFI schedules required.

Dividends, In and Out

A dividend received is income. A dividend paid is a transaction. Either one ends the nil year, and a corporation that did both is firmly outside it.

Work that is not nil is handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year. There are no meetings, no scheduling and no email chains in either direction.

A Holding Corporation Held in Reserve

A corporation incorporated to hold a name or a future structure, holding nothing and earning nothing, is the clearest nil holding case there is. It still files every year.

The maintenance position is set out in the guide to shelf corporation compliance.

Years Already Missed

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

Holding corporations accumulate unfiled years quietly, because nothing happens to prompt anyone. The gap usually surfaces when the structure is being reorganised or wound up, at the point a clearance certificate is needed and cannot be issued.

Winding the Structure Up

Every open year is filed before dissolution, and a final T2 is due within six months of it. A holding corporation sitting at the top of a structure is usually the last to be wound up and the one carrying the longest filing gap.

The order is set out in the guide to the final T2 and dissolution.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a Holding Company a Nil Corporation?

Not where it has investment income. A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

My Holding Company Earned $6 of Interest. Is It Still Nil?

No. There is no minimum. Interest credited on a balance is investment income, and the corporation is not nil for that tax year.

Does an Inactive Holding Company Have to File?

Yes. Every resident corporation, including an inactive one, must file a T2 within six months of its fiscal year-end, every year, until it is formally dissolved.

Does a Holding Company Need the GIFI Schedules?

Almost always. Share capital, cash, a shareholder loan, an incorporation cost or a bank charge makes Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required, and a holding corporation holds assets by definition.

Does an Interest-Free Loan to a Subsidiary End the Nil Year?

An interest-free loan left outstanding across the year, with nothing moving and nothing charged, does not by itself make the year active. It does put a balance on the balance sheet, which makes the GIFI schedules required.

Is Schedule 50 Needed for a Corporate Shareholder?

Yes, where that shareholder holds 10% or more. The row records the shareholding corporation and its business number rather than an individual.

content:

What Decides Which Schedules Are Needed

Not the amount of income, which is $0.00 on every nil return. What the corporation holds, who owns it, and whether this is its first return.

ScheduleDecided by
GIFI 100, 125 and 141What sits on the balance sheet
Schedule 50Who owns 10% or more
Schedule 24Whether this is the first return after incorporation
Schedule 8 and loss continuityWhether there is anything to carry forward

Three of the four have nothing to do with trading, which is why a corporation that did nothing all year still files schedules.

The GIFI Rule, Stated Exactly

A corporation inactive all year with nothing to report may omit GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141, but any share capital, cash, shareholder loan, incorporation cost or bank charge makes them required.

Read the second half carefully. The exemption needs nothing at all to report. A corporation holding $100.00 of share capital issued at incorporation has something to report, and the schedules are required.

The full treatment is in the guide to GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141.

The Five Things That Make GIFI Required

TriggerWhy it counts
Share capitalIssued at incorporation and sits on the balance sheet
CashA balance in an account is an asset
A shareholder loanA balance either owed to or by the corporation
An incorporation costCapitalised, so it remains on the balance sheet
A bank chargeAn expense, so there is something on the income statement

Four of the five are present in most corporations from the day they are registered, which is why the exemption is narrower in practice than it reads.

Schedule 100, the Balance Sheet

The balance sheet in GIFI codes: what the corporation owns, what it owes, and the share capital and retained earnings that make up the difference.

On a nil return it is usually short. Share capital on one line, perhaps a bank balance, perhaps a shareholder loan. Short is not the same as omitted.

Schedule 125, the Income Statement

Revenue and expenses in GIFI codes. On a genuinely nil year both sides are $0.00, and the schedule says so explicitly rather than being left out.

A single bank charge is an expense, and it belongs on Schedule 125. It does not stop the year being nil for this service, but it does mean the schedule is filed.

Schedule 141, the Notes Checklist

The notes checklist records who prepared the financial information and what level of involvement they had. It accompanies Schedules 100 and 125 and is filed with them.

See whether financial statements are needed for a nil T2 return.

Schedule 50, Shareholders at 10% or More

Schedule 50 is needed for any shareholder at 10% or more. It lists each of them, their percentage of common and preferred shares, and their identification number.

The test is ownership of the shares, not involvement in the company. A shareholder who has never attended a meeting still appears where the holding reaches the threshold. The detail is on the Schedule 50 and the 10% shareholder rule post.

Schedule 24, First Return Only

Schedule 24 is needed on the first return after incorporation. It reports the corporation’s shareholders, its related corporations and how it came into existence, and it is filed once.

Where a first year was never filed, Schedule 24 is still filed, late, on whichever return turns out to be the first one transmitted. The detail is in the guide to first-year T2 filing.

Schedule 8 and Loss Continuity

Schedule 8 and loss continuity must be recorded. A nil year adds nothing to either, but the continuity has to be carried forward intact so a later year can use it.

This is the schedule most often skipped on a nil return, and the one that costs the most to skip. A break in loss continuity is discovered in the year the corporation finally has income to apply it against.

The full treatment is in the guide to Schedule 8 and loss continuity.

The T2 Short and Its Schedules

The T2 Short is available only to a CCPC with nil net income or a loss, one permanent establishment, no taxable dividends paid or received, Canadian currency, no refundable credits, no Ontario transitional debit and no section 34.2 amount.

Qualifying for the shorter form does not remove a schedule that is otherwise required. Eligibility is covered in the guide to T2 Short eligibility.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which Schedules Does a Nil T2 Need?

It depends on what the corporation holds rather than what it earned. GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 where there is anything on the balance sheet, Schedule 50 for any shareholder at 10% or more, Schedule 24 on a first return, and Schedule 8 with loss continuity recorded.

Can a Nil Return Skip the GIFI Schedules?

Only where the corporation was inactive all year with nothing at all to report. Any share capital, cash, shareholder loan, incorporation cost or bank charge makes Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required.

Does Share Capital Alone Make GIFI Required?

Yes. Share capital issued at incorporation sits on the balance sheet, which is something to report, so the schedules are required.

Do I Need Schedule 24 Every Year?

No. Schedule 24 is filed once, on the first return after incorporation.

Why File Schedule 8 on a Year With Nothing in It?

To carry the continuity forward intact. A break is only discovered in the year the corporation finally has income to apply a loss against.

Is There an Extra Charge for Schedules?

No. The fee is $300.00 plus HST per tax year and covers whichever schedules the return requires.

What a Shelf Corporation Is

A corporation registered and then held without trading, kept so the name, the incorporation date or the structure is available when it is needed.

It is a dormant corporation with an intention attached. The filing obligations are identical either way, because the Canada Revenue Agency and the corporate registries record what a corporation is, not what it is for.

Three Separate Obligations, Not One

This is where shelf corporations are lost. Filing a T2 satisfies one obligation out of three, and the other two sit with different bodies on different timetables.

FilingFiled withWhen
T2 corporate income tax returnCanada Revenue AgencyWithin six months of the fiscal year-end, every year
Ontario annual returnOntario Business RegistryAnnually, since October 2021, separately from the T2
Federal annual returnCorporations Canada, for a federally incorporated corporationWithin 60 days of the anniversary date, $12.00

A corporation can be perfectly current on its T2 and still be struck from a registry for missing the other two.

The T2, Every Year, Without Exception

Every resident corporation, including an inactive one, must file a T2 within six months of its fiscal year-end, every year, until it is formally dissolved. A final T2 is due within six months of dissolution.

There is no dormant status to elect, no form that pauses the obligation, and no threshold below which it stops. A corporation held on a shelf for nine years owes nine returns.

The Ontario Annual Return

The Ontario annual return is filed through the Ontario Business Registry since October 2021, not with the T2. Before that date it travelled with the corporate tax return, which is why so many corporations stopped filing it without noticing.

A shelf corporation registered before 2021 and left alone since is the exact profile that has an unfiled registry return and no idea of it.

Nil T2 Filing, $300.00 plus HST per tax year

One price for every year and every province. CPA reviewed and transmitted electronically.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

The Federal Annual Return and the $12.00 Fee

Federal corporations file a separate $12.00 Corporations Canada annual return within 60 days of their anniversary. It is not a tax return and it does not report income.

Missing it is what leads to dissolution for cause. A federally incorporated shelf corporation can be dissolved by Corporations Canada while its tax filings are entirely up to date.

Alberta and Quebec Have Their Own Returns

Alberta AT1 and Quebec CO-17 are separate provincial returns. A shelf corporation with a permanent establishment in either province files there as well as federally.

The provincial and federal position is set out in the guide to provincial and federal annual returns.

Open GST/HST and Payroll Accounts

An open GST/HST account or an open payroll account still needs nil filings, or a closure using Form RC145. An inactive T2 does not close those accounts.

A shelf corporation that once registered for GST/HST and never deregistered is accruing a second set of missed filings alongside its T2 years.

Whether the Shelf Year Is Actually Nil

Usually yes, and that is the point of the structure. The exceptions are narrow and worth checking against rather than assuming.

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Interest credited on a dormant bank balance is the common one. It is investment income, and the year is not nil.

What a Shelf Corporation Still Reports

Share capital issued at incorporation sits on the balance sheet from day one, so GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 are required on most shelf returns despite there being no activity.

ScheduleOn a shelf corporation
GIFI 100, 125 and 141Usually required, because share capital exists
Schedule 50Required where any shareholder holds 10% or more
Schedule 24On the first return only
Schedule 8 and loss continuityRecorded, carrying forward unchanged

The full position is in the guide to T2 schedules on a nil return.

A Shelf Corporation With Missed Years

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

Unfiled years are filed oldest first, one return per tax year. Six years held on a shelf and never filed is six returns, prepared and transmitted together.

See filing nil T2 returns for a corporation that was forgotten about.

Before the Corporation Is Used or Sold

A shelf corporation is worth what its record is worth. A buyer, a bank or a lawyer completing a transaction looks at the filing history, and an open year stops the transaction rather than discounting it.

The filings are brought current before the corporation is needed, not during the week it is needed. Catching up six years takes preparation time that a closing date does not leave.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a Shelf Corporation Have to File a T2?

Yes, every year. Every resident corporation, including an inactive one, must file a T2 within six months of its fiscal year-end, every year, until it is formally dissolved.

Is There a Dormant Status I Can Elect?

No. There is no status that pauses the filing obligation and no threshold below which it stops.

Is the Ontario Annual Return Part of the T2?

Not since October 2021. It is filed through the Ontario Business Registry, separately from the corporate tax return.

What Is the $12 Federal Annual Return?

A separate Corporations Canada filing for federally incorporated corporations, due within 60 days of the anniversary date. It is not a tax return, and missing it can lead to dissolution for cause.

My Shelf Corporation Earned Bank Interest. Is It Nil?

No. Interest credited on a balance is investment income, so the year is not nil for this service.

Can I Catch Up Six Years at Once?

Yes. Each year is its own return, filed oldest first, and they are prepared and transmitted together.
